disclaimer: These are general red-flag responses. Follow the crew medical training and the onboard procedures; ORBIT does not replace emergency medical care.

procedures.title: Chest pain or pressure
steps: Stop all activity and stay where you are. Sit or lie down in a secure position.
Alert the crew now and call the flight surgeon or ground medical team on the emergency channel.
Start the crew medical officer's procedure. Do not treat beyond your training.
Keep watching breathing and responsiveness, and note the time the symptoms began.
procedures.escalate: Immediately. Chest pain is always treated as an emergency.
procedures.source: General emergency medical principles; follow the mission's approved onboard medical procedures.

procedures.title: Severe breathing difficulty
steps: Stop all activity and alert the crew immediately.
Check the cabin air and any CO2 alarms. If the air may be the cause, put on your breathing mask and follow the cabin emergency procedure.
Keep the person sitting upright and calm, and use supplemental oxygen only if trained to do so.
Call the flight surgeon or ground medical team now. If the person stops breathing, start CPR as trained.
procedures.escalate: Immediately. Severe breathing difficulty is always treated as an emergency.
procedures.source: General emergency medical principles; cabin atmosphere emergency procedures.

procedures.title: Loss of consciousness
steps: Make sure the area is safe, then alert the crew and call the medical team immediately.
Check breathing and pulse. If there is no normal breathing, start CPR as trained.
Secure the person with restraints to prevent injury, and do not move them unless the area is unsafe.
Keep the medical team informed of changes and note the time of the event.
procedures.escalate: Immediately. Any loss of consciousness is an emergency.
procedures.source: General emergency medical principles; crew CPR and medical training.

procedures.title: Severe bleeding
steps: Apply firm, direct pressure to the wound with sterile gauze or cloth.
If pressure does not control bleeding on a limb, apply a tourniquet if you are trained to do so.
Keep the injured person still and, if possible, raise the injured limb.
Alert the crew and call the medical team now, and keep applying pressure until help arrives.
procedures.escalate: Immediately. Severe bleeding is always treated as an emergency.
procedures.source: General first-aid and trauma principles; follow the onboard medical kit procedures.
